summary: EtherHiding loader in babel.config.cjs fetches and executes attacker JavaScript via Ethereum-resolved C2
details: babel.config.cjs prepends a heavily obfuscated Node.js IIFE after the legitimate Babel presets. The payload queries public Ethereum mainnet RPCs (eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, eth.drpc.org, 1rpc.io/eth, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com) for the latest transaction from sender 0xa322e5f3d311d3080e6f01210633e9aDC2490Ef1a, decodes two IPv4 addresses from the transaction `to` field, downloads XOR-encoded JavaScript from those hosts at paths /0x/cls and /0x/ls, and executes it both via `eval` and via a detached `node -e` spawn. The loader fires whenever Babel or babel-jest evaluates its config, so any `npm test`, jest run, or Babel-driven build against a project including this package triggers full remote code execution. A second copy of the same loader is staged as public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2, a plaintext-JavaScript file disguised with a Font Awesome asset name and unicode-escaped identifiers for `require`, `child_process`, `spawn`, `eval`, and the network destinations. Blockchain-resolved C2 lets the operator rotate destination IPs by publishing a new transaction from the sender address.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
